newsitem.title: USA: Officials mop up fuel spilled on Bering Strait ice.
newsitem.headline: Officials mop up fuel spilled on Bering Strait ice.

text.p: Thick diesel fuel that spilled from storm-damaged storage tanks in a remote Alaska village was being mopped up from the ice along the narrow Bering Strait, federal and state officials said Friday.
The 28,000 gallon spill was from tanks at a U.S. Navy Arctic submarine laboratory near Wales, the Alaska Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) said.

The spill appears to have occurred November 15, but was not reported until Wednesday because telephone lines had been out of operation, DEC said. The Navy station had been closed for the season, DEC said.

Navy and U.S. Coast Guard representatives arrived at the site Thursday to launch a cleanup that was coordinated by DEC. Most of the spilled fuel was stopped by a secondary containment, but about 1,000 gallons escaped.

Wales, on the western tip of the Seward Peninsula and about 650 miles northwest of Anchorage, is an Inupiat Eskimo settlement of about 170 people. It is fewer than 60 miles from the Siberian mainland and is one of the closest Alaska settlements to Russia.
